outcomes.text: Test whether two proposed coordinates can serve the same function in context.
Recognise restrictions on coordinating clause forms and nouns under one determiner.
Trace a supplementary relative clause to its anchor.

key_terms.definition: One member of a pair or series joined at the same structural level.
An expression set apart from the main structure that adds information about an anchor.
The expression, person, thing or situation a supplement comments on.

options.text: Both are subjects of arrived.
options.feedback: Each expression can supply a circumstance of the arrival.

options.text: Both are objects of arrived.
options.feedback: Each expression can supply a circumstance of the arrival.

options.text: They are adjuncts to arrived.
options.feedback: Each expression can supply a circumstance of the arrival.

opening.prompt: In “The crates arrived yesterday and without warning”, what job do the coordinates share?

options.text: Labelling or to photograph the crates would help.
options.feedback: The two clauses in this subject coordination have the same form.

options.text: Labelling or photographing the crates would help.
options.feedback: The two clauses in this subject coordination have the same form.

options.text: To label or photographing the crates would help.
options.feedback: The two clauses in this subject coordination have the same form.

opening.prompt: Which pair makes an ordinary coordination in subject position?

options.text: the large crate
options.feedback: The relative adds an origin detail about the crate.

options.text: Manila
options.feedback: The relative adds an origin detail about the crate.

options.text: was heavy
options.feedback: The relative adds an origin detail about the crate.

opening.prompt: What is the anchor of the supplement in “The large crate, which came from Manila, was heavy”?

options.text: the corridor
options.feedback: Without hesitation can modify spoke independently, just as softly can.

options.text: her voice
options.feedback: Without hesitation can modify spoke independently, just as softly can.

options.text: without hesitation
options.feedback: Without hesitation can modify spoke independently, just as softly can.

opening.prompt: Which second coordinate fits “She spoke softly and ___” as another manner adjunct?

options.text: these cups and saucers
options.feedback: Repeating the singular determiner creates two full phrases. The last option describes plurals.

options.text: this cup and that saucer
options.feedback: Repeating the singular determiner creates two full phrases. The last option describes plurals.

options.text: these cup and saucer
options.feedback: Repeating the singular determiner creates two full phrases. The last option describes plurals.

opening.prompt: Which version names one cup and one saucer with two separate noun phrases?

options.text: sturdy and in good condition
options.feedback: An adjective phrase and a preposition phrase can each describe the parcel after was in the first option.

options.text: sturdy and the lobby
options.feedback: An adjective phrase and a preposition phrase can each describe the parcel after was in the first option.

options.text: at the depot and yesterday morning arrived
options.feedback: An adjective phrase and a preposition phrase can each describe the parcel after was in the first option.

closing.prompt: Which pair can both serve after “The parcel was ___”?

options.text: The parcel arrived undamaged, which was a relief.
options.feedback: The relief comes from the safe arrival, so the preceding clause provides the anchor.

options.text: The parcel which arrived undamaged went upstairs.
options.feedback: The relief comes from the safe arrival, so the preceding clause provides the anchor.

options.text: The parcel, which arrived undamaged, went upstairs.
options.feedback: The relief comes from the safe arrival, so the preceding clause provides the anchor.

closing.prompt: Which sentence has a supplementary relative about the whole reported situation?

options.text: These can select only singular nouns.
options.feedback: The number condition applies to the grammatical head. There can be two objects in the real world and still be two singular nouns in the coordination.

options.text: The two singular nouns do not make a plural head that these can select.
options.feedback: The number condition applies to the grammatical head. There can be two objects in the real world and still be two singular nouns in the coordination.

options.text: The problem is a missing relative clause.
options.feedback: The number condition applies to the grammatical head. There can be two objects in the real world and still be two singular nouns in the coordination.

closing.prompt: Why does “these cup and saucer” fail in the shared-determiner construction?

options.text: Which had been relabelled, arrived first.
options.feedback: The supplement is set off after its anchor. The integrated alternative can help identify which crate.

options.text: The crate which had been relabelled arrived first.
options.feedback: The supplement is set off after its anchor. The integrated alternative can help identify which crate.

options.text: The blue crate, which had been relabelled, arrived first.
options.feedback: The supplement is set off after its anchor. The integrated alternative can help identify which crate.

closing.prompt: Which wording treats “which had been relabelled” as an added comment about an already identified crate?

options.text: Check that both phrases have the same spelling pattern.
options.feedback: The independent readings show that both can serve as adjuncts.

options.feedback: The independent readings show that both can serve as adjuncts.

options.text: Read each part after arrived on its own.
options.feedback: The independent readings show that both can serve as adjuncts.
